- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to capture mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts and forecasts higher than true; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias in second half of horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply upward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/0.67 alternation, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% ahead of true price in early days.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often misses mean reversion; add 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or bearish in last 3–5 days.
